$comment: The data-connectors commit the managed-connector end-to-end job builds its test artifact from.
WHY A PIN RATHER THAN A BRANCH NAME. Cross-repo SHA pinning is the established convention
between these two repos, in the OTHER direction: data-connectors records a data-connect SHA in
ITS OWN .github/cross-repo-pins.json, which this repo's consumer-drift-signal.yml reads by raw
fetch from that repo's main. NOTE that no cross-repo-pins.json exists in THIS repo — the file
this pin is modelled on lives in data-connectors, so this is the same idea pointed the other way,
not an edit to an existing local file. Same reasoning applies in this direction: the job asserts
that this repo's consumer can read the artifact data-connectors' builder ACTUALLY emits, so the
producer revision has to be a fact recorded in the tree, not whatever a moving branch means on
the day CI runs. A moving ref would turn a producer-side change into a mystery failure here.
WHY THIS REVISION. bd6f94a1 is data-connectors' main commit for PR #216 (2026-09-26). Its builder
emits the source declaration, which the installer this repo pins requires (@opendatalabs/
data-connectors-tools at 06f79d58, packages/local-collector/package.json). It publishes the
declaration as an OCI referrer of the connector image, not as an image layer. An earlier revision,
5fa1e7bb3f (PR #212), put the declaration in the image as a layer, and this repo's managed artifact
contract (packages/local-collector/src/managed/artifact-contract.ts) refuses a layer it does not know,
so #212 artifacts fail the live-registry test here. The referrer keeps the image to the layers every
consumer knows, which is the reason the publish workflow gives for the change.
A MERGED COMMIT, NOT A PR HEAD. A commit on main cannot be made unreachable by a force-push, which
is the weakness of pinning a PR head. The job still fails at fetch, with a clear message, if the
commit is ever removed from the repository.
WHY connector IS STILL oura WHEN THE PUBLISH PILOT IS ynab. The publish workflow at this revision
uses ynab as its pilot, and says why: oura would prove the build but not the collection path. That
reasoning is about which connector can be taken to REAL RECORDS end to end. It does not transfer to
this job, which uses no credential and asserts only that the artifact installs and its entrypoint
imports, a claim oura supports as well. Keeping oura keeps this job's meaning stable across the pilot.
THE VERSION IS THE MANIFEST'S VERSION AT THIS REVISION. The builder refuses a --version that
contradicts the manifest, so this version and the version the live-registry test asks for
(managed-connectors-live-registry.test.ts) change together.
IMPORTANT, IF YOU CHANGE connector HERE: this key alone is NOT sufficient. The test body in
packages/local-collector/test/managed-connectors-live-registry.test.ts hardcodes the oura
connectorKey, connector_id, version and the collectOura export name; the workflow parameterises
only the BUILD and PUSH from this file. Setting connector to ynab here would build and push ynab
and then fail in the test against oura's identity. Switching pilots means editing the test too.
